checkpoint_review: The Router was generally accurate but slightly lenient on the 'Label shows...' checkpoint. While it marked it 'untestable' due to resolution, the expert evidence (image_text_auditor returning empty blocks) confirms that the text is not just blurry but effectively non-existent/gibberish. This is a failure of the functional component (legible label), not just an occlusion issue. The Router correctly identified the geometric presence of the cans. The 'Spray nozzle' checkpoint being untestable is acceptable given the caps are on.
artifact_review: The Router's identification of 'text_gibberish' (Severity 3) is supported by the image_text_auditor's failure to extract any text. The 'structural_collapse' of the foreground brush (Severity 2) is visually confirmed; the bristles are a melted mass. The 'fusion' at the base of bottles (Severity 2) is subtle but present, indicated by the lack of crisp contact shadows. The Router did not miss major artifacts, but the severity of the text artifact is critical for product packaging images.
alignment_reasoning: The fine_grained_classifier strongly confirms the class as 'hair spray' (Top-1 logit 8.72 vs 4.08 for next best). The primary subjects (aerosol cans) are geometrically correct and present. However, the alignment is penalized because the 'label' functional component is effectively missing due to AI text generation failure (gibberish), which is a key part of the taxonomy definition ('Surface is printed with brand name...').
artifact_reasoning: Significant artifacts detected. 1) Text Gibberish: All labels are illegible scribbles (Severity 3), confirmed by OCR failure. 2) Structural Melting: Foreground objects like the pink brush have lost their fine structural detail (bristles merged into a blob) (Severity 2-3). 3) Boundary Fusion: Slight bleeding of objects into the table surface (Severity 2). These artifacts prevent the image from achieving high quality scores despite good global geometry.
key_defects: Illegible/Gibberish text on all product labels
